intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the bustling 36 streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter on foot, sampling iconic dishes like Bun Cha, Banh Mi, and Egg Coffee from local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Stay in a hostel within the Old Quarter itself to maximize time and minimize transit on arrival day. Since the flight arrives late, this low-key evening stroll is perfect for Day 1 — no booking required, just step outside your door.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Street Food Trail
experiences.description: Wander through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An during the monthly Lantern Festival, tasting White Rose Dumplings, Cao Lau noodles, and Banh Mi Phuong from street stalls. Book a guesthouse on Tran Phu Street or Nguyen Thai Hoc Street to be within walking distance of all activity hubs, avoiding costly and time-consuming taxi rides.

experiences.name: Hue Imperial Citadel & Local Com Hen Lunch
experiences.description: Spend a morning cycling around the Hue Imperial Citadel and Royal Tombs, then stop for a bowl of Com Hen (baby clam rice) at a local market stall — a Hue specialty costing under $2. Stay in a budget guesthouse on Hung Vuong Street near the citadel to cut transit time and keep costs low for backpackers.

experiences.name: Ho Chi Minh City Ben Thanh Market & Backpacker Street Experience
experiences.description: Dive into the sensory overload of Ben Thanh Market for fresh produce, local snacks, and souvenirs, then head to Bui Vien Walking Street for an authentic backpacker nightlife experience with cheap street food and live music. Choose a hostel on De Tham Street — the heart of the backpacker district — so everything is walkable from your accommodation.
experiences.location: Backpacker District (Pham Ngu Lao), Ho Chi Minh City

experiences.name: Ninh Binh Tam Coc Boat Ride & Village Cycling
experiences.description: Take a scenic 2-hour sampan boat ride through the limestone karst caves of Tam Coc, then rent a bicycle ($2/day) to explore Bich Dong Pagoda and local rice paddies. Stay in a guesthouse in Tam Coc village itself rather than in Ninh Binh city center — this cuts a 9km commute each way and ensures you can start early before tour crowds arrive.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly 86 Express Bus (45,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check in to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, freshen up, and take a slow orientation walk through the narrow streets of the 36 Ancient Streets district. Get your bearings around Hoan Kiem Lake (15-min walk from most Old Quarter guesthouses).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Hoan Kiem Lake for the iconic view of Ngoc Son Temple lit up at dusk. Head into the buzzing Bia Hoi Corner (Hang Buom & Ta Hien St junction) for a glass of fresh draught beer (10,000–15,000 VND). Explore the night market on Hang Dao Street (open Fri–Sun) or simply wander the lantern-lit alleys.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab Banh Mi from a street cart near the airport or Old Quarter on arrival (~25,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Cha (grilled pork with rice noodles) at a street-side stall on Hang Manh or Le Van Huu Street (~50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport (avoid hotel rates). Grab a local SIM card (Viettel or Vietnamobile) for ~100,000 VND with data. Keep small bills handy for street food.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:00–7:00 AM) to witness locals doing Tai Chi exercises around Hoan Kiem Lake – a truly authentic Hanoi moment. Visit Ngoc Son Temple on the lake (30,000 VND entry). Afterward, head to the nearby St. Joseph's Cathedral for a look at the French colonial architecture (free entry during open hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) – Vietnam's first university, dating to 1070 (30,000 VND entry). Walk or take a Grab bike (~30,000 VND) to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex area. Explore the One Pillar Pagoda (free) and the exterior of the Presidential Palace. Visit Ho Chi Minh Museum (40,000 VND) for deep cultural context.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter for the famous Pho experience. Join a free walking tour run by local university students (tip-based, ~50,000 VND tip recommended) – check noticeboards at your hostel. End the night with egg coffee (Ca Phe Trung) at Cafe Dinh or Giang Cafe on Nguyen Huu Huan Street (~30,000 VND) – a Hanoi specialty.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor near Hoan Kiem Lake (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Binh Dan (budget rice plate with multiple toppings) on Hang Bong Street (~40,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) at Pho Thin on Lo Duc Street or a local pho stall (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays, and during certain national events. Dress modestly when visiting temples and pagodas. Carry a small daypack for water and snacks.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 – April 17 (Hanoi Hidden Gems & Street Food Tour)
day_by_day.morning: Explore the Dong Xuan Market – Hanoi's largest covered market – for a glimpse into local wholesale trade and everyday life (free entry). Browse the surrounding streets for cheap clothing, souvenirs, and local snacks. Walk along the famous Train Street (Phung Hung Street) to see houses inches from the railway tracks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (60,000 VND) – one of the best museums in Southeast Asia, showcasing 54 ethnic minority groups. Take a Grab bike (~40,000 VND one way). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the outdoor and indoor exhibits. Head back toward the Old Quarter and visit Hoa Lo Prison (Hanoi Hilton) (30,000 VND) for a sobering historical perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Join a self-guided street food crawl through the Old Quarter. Try multiple dishes from different vendors. Walk along Ma May and Hang Be Streets for the best concentration of street food stalls. Finish with a Bia Hoi session at the corner junction.

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) at a street stall on Hang Ga Street (~30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodles) at a local restaurant on Hang Dieu Street (~50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food crawl: Nem Ran (fried spring rolls, ~20,000 VND), Banh Mi (~25,000 VND), Che (sweet dessert soup, ~15,000 VND) – total ~60,000–80,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: The Train Street has become touristy – visit early morning or late afternoon for the best experience and to avoid crowds. Always check train schedules if visiting Train Street for safety.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station to Ninh Binh (~2.5 hours, ~80,000–100,000 VND). Alternatively, book a budget day tour from the Old Quarter (~250,000–350,000 VND including transport). Arrive and rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) to explore at your own pace. Visit Trang An Grottoes Landscape Complex – a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Take a 2-hour boat ride through limestone karsts and caves (250,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Hoa Lu Ancient Capital (20,000 VND entry) – the 10th-century capital of Vietnam with beautiful temples. Continue cycling to Mua Cave – climb 500 steps to the dragon spine ridge for panoramic views over the rice paddies and karst mountains (100,000 VND entry). The view is worth every step.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Ninh Binh town for dinner before catching the late bus back to Hanoi. Arrive in Hanoi by 9:00–10:00 PM. Relax at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure or grab Banh Mi at the bus station (~25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Chay (crispy rice with goat meat or pork) – a Ninh Binh specialty at a local restaurant (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: De Nui (mountain goat hot pot) at a local Ninh Binh eatery before the return bus (~80,000–100,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Start early (6:00–7:00 AM departure) to maximize time in Ninh Binh. Wear comfortable shoes for the Mua Cave climb. Bring sunscreen and water. This is a long day – pack light.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – April 19 (Travel Day: Hanoi to Hoi An via Sleeper Train/Bus)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hanoi accommodation. Depending on train/bus booking: Option A – Take the overnight sleeper train from Hanoi to Da Nang (departs evening, ~16 hours, soft sleeper ~350,000–500,000 VND). Option B – Take a budget flight to Da Nang (book in advance, ~500,000–800,000 VND on VietJet or Bamboo). Spend the morning doing any last-minute Hanoi exploration – revisit Hoan Kiem Lake or pick up snacks for the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Store luggage at the hotel or a luggage storage spot (~20,000–30,000 VND). Visit the Fine Arts Museum of Vietnam (40,000 VND) near the Temple of Literature for a final cultural stop. Grab supplies for the overnight journey: water, instant noodles, snacks from a local convenience store.
day_by_day.evening: Board the sleeper train or evening bus to Da Nang/Hoi An. Settle in for the overnight journey. The train ride itself is an experience – passing through coastal scenery and mountain passes.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Xeo (turmeric sticky rice with mung bean) from a street cart (~25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun Cha or Com Binh Dan for a final Hanoi meal (~50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Train/bus station food or packed snacks purchased beforehand (~30,000–50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets in advance at baolau.com or 12go.asia. Soft sleeper berths are worth the small price premium for comfort. Keep valuables secure in your daypack while sleeping on the train.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 – April 20 (Arrive Hoi An: Ancient Town Exploration)
day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Da Nang by train/bus. Take a local bus (Route 1) or shared taxi to Hoi An (~30–45 mins, bus ~30,000 VND, shared taxi ~100,000 VND). Check in to a budget guesthouse in or near Hoi An Ancient Town. Freshen up and head straight to the UNESCO-listed Hoi An Ancient Town. Purchase the Ancient Town ticket (120,000 VND for 5 attraction tickets) and start with the Japanese Covered Bridge – the town's iconic symbol.
day_by_day.afternoon: Use your Ancient Town tickets to visit the Tan Ky Old House (a beautifully preserved 200-year-old merchant home) and the Fujian Chinese Assembly Hall. Wander the atmospheric yellow-walled streets, browse local art galleries and tailors. Walk along the Thu Bon River and watch local fishermen at work.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Hoi An's magical lantern-lit evening – the Ancient Town transforms after dark. Head to the riverside for floating lanterns (release a lantern for ~20,000–30,000 VND for good luck). Browse the Night Market on Nguyen Hoang Street for souvenirs and local snacks.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the train/bus or grab Banh Mi upon arrival in Hoi An (~25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish) at Thanh Cao Lau or a local stall (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Com Ga Hoi An (Hoi An chicken rice) at Ba Buoi restaurant – a local institution (~60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An Ancient Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle. Rent a bicycle from your guesthouse (~50,000 VND/day). The town is most beautiful in the evening when lanterns are lit. If visiting on the 14th or 15th of the lunar month, the Full Moon Lantern Festival is spectacular.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 – April 21 (Hoi An: Beaches, Cooking & Countryside)
day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle and cycle 4km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach – some of Central Vietnam's most beautiful stretches of sand. Enjoy a morning swim and relax. Beach entry is free; just pay for a sun lounger if desired (~50,000 VND) or lay on the free public beach area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget cooking class (look for classes around 200,000–350,000 VND at Morning Glory Cooking School or similar) – learn to make Cao Lau, White Rose Dumplings, and fresh spring rolls. Alternatively, cycle into the countryside along the Thu Bon River to visit local villages and rice paddies – a completely free and rewarding experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Ancient Town for a final evening stroll. Visit the Hoi An Market (Cho Hoi An) for fresh produce and street food. Try White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Fried Wontons from street vendors. Grab a cheap beer at a riverside bar and watch the lanterns reflect on the water.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong – famous banh mi spot on Phan Chau Trinh Street (~30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at An Bang Beach – grilled corn, fresh coconut, and a simple fish dish (~80,000–100,000 VND total)
meals.dinner: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with pork and shrimp) at a local stall in the market (~40,000–50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Banh Mi Phuong is world-famous (featured by Anthony Bourdain) – arrive early to avoid queues. Cycling to the beach takes about 20–30 minutes and is a lovely ride through rural scenery. Apply sunscreen generously – the Central Vietnam sun is strong.

day_by_day.date: Day 8 – April 22 (Travel Day: Hoi An to Ho Chi Minh City + Arrival)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hoi An guesthouse. Take a local bus or taxi to Da Nang Airport (~45 mins). Fly to Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Son Nhat Airport) – book budget airlines (VietJet, Bamboo) in advance for ~400,000–700,000 VND. Alternatively, take an overnight sleeper bus from Hoi An directly to HCMC (~12 hours, ~200,000–300,000 VND) – departs evening, saving a night's accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Take the 109 Airport Bus to the city center (~20,000 VND) or a Grab bike (~80,000–100,000 VND). Check in to a budget guesthouse or hostel in District 1 (Pham Ngu Lao backpacker area). Drop bags and head out for an initial orientation walk around Ben Thanh Market area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker street – grab a cheap beer at a sidewalk plastic-stool bar. Walk to the iconic Ben Thanh Market Night Market for street food and souvenirs. Visit Nguyen Hue Walking Street – a wide pedestrian boulevard lined with cafes and street performers.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Banh Mi at a Hoi An street stall before departure (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Airport food or packed snacks (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes) at a street stall near Pham Ngu Lao (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book flights well in advance for the best budget prices. Tan Son Nhat Airport is busy – allow extra time. The Pham Ngu Lao area (District 1) is the classic backpacker hub with the cheapest dorm beds (100,000–150,000 VND/night) and budget guesthouses.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 – April 23 (Ho Chi Minh City: History, Culture & Street Food)
day_by_day.morning: Start with the War Remnants Museum (40,000 VND) – one of the most powerful and moving museums in Southeast Asia, documenting the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective. Allow 2 hours. Walk to the Reunification Palace (formerly the Presidential Palace) (40,000 VND) – explore the underground war bunkers and retro 1960s interiors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Notre-Dame Cathedral (free exterior viewing) and the iconic French colonial Central Post Office (free entry) – still functioning, with beautiful architecture. Take a Grab bike to Cho Lon (Chinatown) in District 5 (~30,000 VND) – explore Binh Tay Market and the ornate Thien Hau Pagoda (free). This is authentic, non-touristy Saigon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to District 1 for the famous Saigon street food experience. Head to Bui Vien Walking Street (known as 'Crazy Street') for the wild nightlife atmosphere – cheap beer, live music, and street food. Alternatively, for a more local experience, grab plastic stools at a sidewalk restaurant on De Tham Street.

meals.breakfast: Hu Tieu (Southern-style noodle soup) from a street cart near the guesthouse (~40,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) – Saigon's signature dish at a local Com Tam stall (~50,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Thit Nuong (grilled pork vermicelli) or Banh Mi from a Pham Ngu Lao street vendor (~40,000–60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum is emotionally heavy – be prepared. Cho Lon is best explored by motorbike taxi or Grab for speed. Bui Vien Street is very touristy but fun for one night – for a more local nightlife experience, explore side streets off Pham Ngu Lao.

day_by_day.date: Day 10 – April 24 (Day Trip: Cu Chi Tunnels & Farewell Saigon)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~40km northwest of HCMC). Options: Budget local bus (Route 13 from Ben Thanh, ~20,000 VND) + local bus (~15,000 VND) – total ~2 hours. Or join a budget group tour (~150,000–200,000 VND including transport). Entry to Ben Dinh tunnels: 110,000 VND. Crawl through the narrow tunnels, see booby traps, and learn about the remarkable Viet Cong underground network.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ho Chi Minh City by early afternoon. Use remaining time for last-minute souvenir shopping at Ben Thanh Market (practice your bargaining skills!) or the cheaper Binh Tay Market in Chinatown. Visit the Jade Emperor Pagoda (free) – one of Saigon's most atmospheric temples, filled with incense smoke and intricate woodcarvings.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vietnam – treat yourself to a slightly upgraded dinner (still budget-friendly). Sit at a rooftop cafe for Saigon skyline views. Take a final walk along the Saigon River waterfront at Ton Duc Thang Street. Reflect on the journey over a last glass of Saigon beer (~15,000–20,000 VND from a street vendor). Pack bags for departure.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or Xoi from a street cart near the guesthouse (~25,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Snacks at Cu Chi Tunnels or a local quan an (eatery) on the way back (~50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a farewell meal: Lau (Vietnamese hot pot) for two at a local restaurant (~150,000–200,000 VND total) or fresh seafood at a Binh Dong floating market restaurant (~100,000–150,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book Cu Chi Tunnels transport the night before. Wear old clothes to Cu Chi – the tunnels are dirty. Bring insect repellent. For departure logistics, allow at least 3 hours before international flights from Tan Son Nhat. The 109 Airport Bus is the cheapest option back to the airport (~20,000 VND).

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take an airport taxi or Grab car (~45 min, ~250,000 VND) to your boutique hotel in the Old Quarter. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely self-guided walk through the 36 Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and the bustling maze of narrow lanes. Stop at St. Joseph's Cathedral for photos and soak in the colonial atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hoan Kiem Lake for the evening stroll — watch locals exercise and socialize around the lake. Cross the iconic red Huc Bridge to visit Ngoc Son Temple (Jade Mountain Temple, open until ~18:00). End the night exploring the Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha Huong Lien (Obama's Bun Cha) — try the famous grilled pork and noodle dish that put Hanoi on the culinary map (~60,000–80,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Pho Thin on Lo Duc Street or a bowl of Pho at a local Old Quarter spot (~50,000–70,000 VND). Follow up with egg coffee (Ca Phe Trung) at Cafe Giang, a Hanoi institution.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a local bank in the Old Quarter. Grab a local SIM card (Viettel or Vietnamobile) at the airport for ~150,000 VND with data. Jet lag may set in — keep Day 1 light.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex early (open ~07:30–10:30, closed Mon/Fri). See the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the serene One Pillar Pagoda nearby. Dress modestly — shoulders and knees covered required.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND entry) — one of Southeast Asia's best ethnographic museums showcasing the 54 ethnic groups of Vietnam. Spend 2–3 hours here. Take a Grab back toward the Old Quarter.
day_by_day.evening: Discover the Hanoi Old Quarter's vibrant street food scene on a self-guided food walk. Wander Ta Hien Street (Beer Corner) for a cold Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND per glass) and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a street cart near your hotel (~25,000–35,000 VND) — a crispy baguette stuffed with pate, cold cuts, and fresh herbs.
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle salad) at a local restaurant near the museum (~60,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong — Hanoi's iconic turmeric-marinated fish with dill and noodles (~150,000–200,000 VND per person). A must-try cultural dish.

day_by_day.notes: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays, and for about 2 months annually (Sep–Nov) for maintenance — verify dates before visiting. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh — book a budget day tour or take a bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat station (~2 hours, ~100,000 VND). Visit Trang An Landscape Complex (UNESCO World Heritage Site) — take a 2-hour rowing boat tour through limestone caves and rice paddies (~200,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb Mua Cave (Hang Mua) for a panoramic view over the Tam Coc valley — about 500 steps but absolutely worth it (~100,000 VND entry). Explore Bich Dong Pagoda carved into a limestone cliff.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by early evening. Relax and explore the Old Quarter night scene. Visit Dong Xuan Market — Hanoi's largest covered market — for souvenirs and local goods.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor near the hotel (~20,000–30,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Com Nieu (clay pot rice) with grilled meat and local vegetables at a restaurant in Ninh Binh (~80,000–120,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Bun Rieu (crab and tomato noodle soup) at a local Old Quarter eatery (~50,000–70,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Ninh Binh is best visited on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds. Bring sunscreen and a hat — the Mua Cave climb is exposed to the sun. Renting a bicycle in Ninh Binh (~50,000 VND/day) is a great way to get around if doing it independently.

day_by_day.morning: Take an overnight or early morning sleeper train/bus to Hue (book in advance — ~200,000–350,000 VND for a soft seat or sleeper). Alternatively, fly (~45 min, budget airlines ~500,000–800,000 VND). Arrive in Hue mid-morning and check into a mid-range guesthouse near the Citadel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Imperial Citadel of Hue (UNESCO World Heritage Site, ~150,000 VND entry). Walk through the Ngo Mon Gate, Thai Hoa Palace, and the Forbidden Purple City. Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) to explore the surrounding moat and walls.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Perfume River at sunset. Visit Trang Tien Bridge illuminated at night. Explore Dong Ba Market for local crafts and street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Quick snack or coffee on the train/bus, or grab Banh Mi upon arrival in Hue.
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup) — the dish was born here and is far superior to versions elsewhere (~50,000–70,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Com Hen (baby clam rice) or Banh Khoai (Hue sizzling pancake) at a local restaurant near the Citadel (~80,000–120,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Hue's cuisine is considered the most refined in Vietnam — make the most of it. The city is compact and very bikeable. April weather in Hue can be warm and occasionally rainy — carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike or join a small group tour to explore the Royal Tombs of Hue. Visit the Tomb of Tu Duc (most scenic, set in a pine forest by a lake) and the Tomb of Khai Dinh (dramatic hilltop fusion of Vietnamese and European architecture). ~100,000 VND per tomb.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the legendary Hai Van Pass (Cloud Pass) toward Da Nang — one of the most scenic coastal mountain roads in Southeast Asia. Stop at the old French bunker at the summit for panoramic views. Arrive in Da Nang and check into a mid-range hotel near the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along My Khe Beach at sunset — one of the finest urban beaches in Asia. Cross the iconic Dragon Bridge (Cau Rong) on foot; if visiting on a weekend, the dragon breathes fire and water at 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Banh Canh (thick noodle soup) at a local Hue street stall (~40,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch or stop at a roadside stall on the Hai Van Pass route.
meals.dinner: Mi Quang (Da Nang's signature turmeric noodle dish with shrimp, pork, and herbs) at a local restaurant (~60,000–80,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Renting a motorbike for the Hai Van Pass is an iconic backpacker experience (~150,000–200,000 VND/day). Alternatively, hire a private car or join a tour. The pass road is winding — drive carefully. Luggage can be sent ahead by bus.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hoi An Ancient Town (~30 km south of Da Nang, ~100,000 VND by Grab or local bus). Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot — visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, Phung Hung Old House, and Fujian Chinese Assembly Hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a cooking class in Hoi An (~300,000–500,000 VND) — learn to make Cao Lau, White Rose Dumplings, and Banh Mi. Many classes include a market tour. Alternatively, browse the tailors on Tran Phu Street for custom-made clothing (a Hoi An specialty).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hoi An for the magical lantern-lit evening — the Ancient Town glows beautifully after dark. Release a lantern on the Thu Bon River (~20,000–30,000 VND). Browse the night market for souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong — widely considered Vietnam's best Banh Mi (~30,000–40,000 VND). Get there early as queues form fast.
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An's unique thick noodle dish made with local well water) at a riverside restaurant (~60,000–80,000 VND).
meals.dinner: White Rose Dumplings and Fried Wonton at Hai Cafe or a local restaurant in the Ancient Town (~100,000–150,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An Ancient Town entry tickets (~120,000 VND) give access to 5 heritage sites. The town is very walkable and bike-friendly. Avoid the hottest midday hours by taking a break at a riverside cafe. Return to Da Nang by late evening or consider staying the night in Hoi An.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC/Saigon) — budget airlines (VietJet, Bamboo) from ~500,000–900,000 VND, ~1 hour flight. Check into a mid-range hotel in District 1 (Bui Vien area or Ben Thanh Market vicinity).
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into HCMC history at the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — one of the most powerful and sobering museums in Southeast Asia. Follow with a visit to the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND), where the Vietnam War effectively ended in 1975.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the legendary Bui Vien Walking Street — HCMC's backpacker hub alive with bars, street food, and live music. Experience the chaotic energy of Saigon at night.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick Banh Mi or Pho at the airport or upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork chop, fried egg, and pickled vegetables) — HCMC's most iconic dish (~50,000–70,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Banh Xeo (sizzling Vietnamese crepe stuffed with shrimp, pork, and bean sprouts) at a local restaurant on Dinh Cong Trang Street (~80,000–120,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: HCMC traffic is intense — use Grab for getting around. District 1 is very walkable for the main sights. The War Remnants Museum is emotionally heavy — allow time to process. Book flights in advance for the best budget fares.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~40 km northwest, ~1.5 hours). Join a half-day tour (~200,000–350,000 VND including transport) to explore the 250 km network of underground tunnels used during the Vietnam War. Crawl through sections of the tunnels and learn about guerrilla warfare tactics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC. Visit Ben Thanh Market for a sensory overload of street food, clothing, and souvenirs. Practice bargaining — it's expected. Explore the surrounding streets for local cafes and shops.
day_by_day.evening: Take a street food tour of HCMC on foot or by cyclo (traditional pedicab). Visit a rooftop bar for cocktails with a skyline view — Chill Sky Bar or similar mid-range option (~100,000–200,000 VND for a drink).

meals.breakfast: Hu Tieu (Southern Vietnamese noodle soup with pork and seafood) at a local street stall (~50,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Snacks and street food at Ben Thanh Market — try Banh Trang Nuong (Vietnamese grilled rice paper pizza, ~20,000–30,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Pho 2000 near Ben Thanh Market (famous for being where President Clinton ate in 2000) or a local Pho spot (~80,000–100,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Cu Chi Tunnels Ben Dinh site is slightly less touristy than Ben Duoc — worth specifying when booking. Bring insect repellent and wear dark clothing (the tunnels are tight and dusty). Comfortable shoes are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Mekong Delta — join a guided day tour from HCMC (~350,000–500,000 VND). Visit My Tho or Ben Tre province. Take a sampan boat through narrow canals lined with coconut palms, visit a coconut candy workshop, and see floating markets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Mekong Delta experience — cycle through fruit orchards, taste tropical fruits (dragon fruit, rambutan, jackfruit), and visit a local family home for insight into rural Vietnamese life. Listen to traditional Don Ca Tai Tu (Southern Vietnamese folk music).
day_by_day.evening: Return to HCMC by late afternoon. Spend the final evening in Saigon exploring the Dong Khoi Street area — browse the Saigon Central Post Office (a stunning French colonial building) and Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon (exterior only if under renovation).

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls with minced pork and mushrooms) at a local HCMC street stall (~40,000–60,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood and local specialties included in most Mekong Delta tours, or a riverside restaurant (~100,000–150,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range Vietnamese restaurant — try Nha Hang Ngon (famous for its courtyard setting and diverse Vietnamese dishes, ~150,000–250,000 VND per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Mekong Delta is best explored with a guide who speaks the local language. Avoid peak tourist hours at floating markets (they're most active before 08:00, so an overnight stay in Can Tho would be ideal for purists). Day trips still offer a great taste of the region.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in HCMC — revisit any favorite spots or do last-minute souvenir shopping at Ben Thanh Market or the Saigon Square mall. Visit the Fine Arts Museum of Ho Chi Minh City (~30,000 VND) — a beautiful French colonial building housing Vietnamese art from the 20th century to present.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final Vietnamese iced coffee (Ca Phe Sua Da) at a local cafe. Pack up and head to Tan Son Nhat International Airport via Grab (~30–45 min from District 1, ~150,000–200,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Ho Chi Minh City. Reflect on 10 incredible days across Vietnam's north, center, and south.

meals.breakfast: Bun Thit Nuong (grilled pork vermicelli bowl with fresh herbs and fish sauce) at a local HCMC eatery (~50,000–70,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or airport — Goi Cuon (fresh spring rolls with shrimp and herbs, ~40,000–60,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner before departure.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Vietnamese Dong (VND) cannot easily be converted back abroad — spend remaining cash or exchange at the airport. Bring home vacuum-packed Vietnamese coffee, pho spice kits, and lacquerware as souvenirs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Private luxury transfer arranged to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, Hanoi. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through the iconic 36 Streets of the Old Quarter – explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and soak in the colonial French architecture and vibrant market energy.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk around Hoan Kiem Lake and visit the illuminated Ngoc Son Temple on Jade Island. Enjoy a welcome cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the lake before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cha Ca Thang Long – a heritage restaurant famous for Hanoi's iconic turmeric-marinated grilled fish dish, Cha Ca La Vong, served tableside with dill and vermicelli. Pair with premium Vietnamese craft beer or rice wine.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport pickup in advance with a premium car service. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Exchange some currency or use hotel concierge for VND cash.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Tai Chi session by Hoan Kiem Lake with locals – a quintessential Hanoi experience. Follow with a guided walking tour of the Old Quarter's most photogenic streets, including a visit to the ancient Bach Ma Temple (White Horse Temple), one of Hanoi's oldest sacred sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) – Vietnam's first university dating to 1070 – followed by the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex and the Presidential Palace gardens. Explore the Ho Chi Minh Museum for cultural depth.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre – a UNESCO-recognized art form unique to northern Vietnam. Stroll through the vibrant Night Market on Hang Dao Street afterward.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) at Pho Thin – a legendary Old Quarter institution open since 1955, famous for its stir-fried beef pho style.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha at Bun Cha Huong Lien (the 'Obama restaurant') – grilled pork patties with vermicelli noodles, made famous by Anthony Bourdain's visit.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at La Badiane – a French-Vietnamese fusion restaurant housed in a stunning colonial villa, offering a seasonal tasting menu with wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays. Book Water Puppet Theatre tickets in advance through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Hoa Lo Prison Museum (the 'Hanoi Hilton') for a powerful historical perspective. Continue to St. Joseph's Cathedral in the French Quarter for architecture photography. Explore the vibrant Dong Xuan Market – Hanoi's largest covered market – with a local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology – one of Southeast Asia's finest ethnographic museums showcasing all 54 ethnic groups of Vietnam. Spend 2–3 hours exploring indoor galleries and outdoor traditional house replicas.
day_by_day.evening: Private street food tour of the Old Quarter by cyclo (rickshaw) – visit hidden alleyway stalls for Banh Mi, Nem Ran (fried spring rolls), Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls), and local Bia Hoi (draft beer) at a street corner.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi at Banh Mi 25 – widely regarded as one of Hanoi's best, with perfectly crispy baguettes and premium fillings.
meals.lunch: Bun Rieu Cua (crab noodle soup) at a local Old Quarter specialty shop recommended by your hotel concierge.
meals.dinner: Premium street food crawl – curated tasting experience through Old Quarter alleys, ending with Egg Coffee (Ca Phe Trung) at Cafe Giang, the original inventor of this Hanoi specialty.

day_by_day.notes: The street food evening tour is best booked through a reputable local guide service. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Egg Coffee at Cafe Giang is a must-try – it's a thick, creamy whipped egg yolk foam over strong Vietnamese coffee.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hanoi hotel. Private luxury transfer (approximately 3.5 hours) to Ha Long Bay pier. En route, stop at a traditional lacquerware workshop in the countryside to observe artisans at work.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a premium overnight cruise (5-star junk boat recommended: Indochine Premium or Paradise Elegance). Sail through the UNESCO World Heritage limestone karst landscape. Kayaking through hidden lagoons and sea caves in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the sundeck as the karsts glow golden. Onboard cooking class learning to make fresh Vietnamese spring rolls and seafood dishes. Multi-course Vietnamese seafood dinner prepared with freshly caught local catch.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Hanoi Boutique Stay before departure.
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch onboard the cruise featuring Vietnamese set menu with fresh seafood – calamari, prawns, and steamed clams.
meals.dinner: Gourmet multi-course seafood dinner onboard – lobster, grilled fish, crab, and seasonal vegetables paired with Vietnamese wine or premium imported bottles.

day_by_day.notes: Book a premium 2-day/1-night or 3-day/2-night Ha Long Bay cruise well in advance. Choose a boat with maximum 20 cabins for exclusivity. Pack light for the cruise – leave large luggage in Hanoi storage.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Tai Chi on the sundeck at sunrise over the karsts. Kayaking or bamboo boat ride through Luon Cave and floating fishing villages. Visit a pearl farm to learn about Ha Long's pearl cultivation industry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final brunch onboard as the cruise returns to port. Private transfer back to Hanoi, then onward to Noi Bai Airport for evening domestic flight to Hoi An (via Da Nang).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive Da Nang Airport, private transfer to Hoi An (approximately 45 minutes). Check in to luxury boutique hotel in Hoi An Ancient Town area. Evening stroll through the lantern-lit Ancient Town.

meals.breakfast: Freshly prepared Vietnamese breakfast onboard – Pho, Banh Mi, tropical fruits, and strong Vietnamese coffee.
meals.lunch: Farewell brunch onboard with Vietnamese and Western options.
meals.dinner: First dinner in Hoi An at The Cargo Club – a beloved riverfront restaurant with a stunning rooftop terrace, serving refined Vietnamese and French cuisine with views over the Thu Bon River.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm domestic flight booking Hanoi to Da Nang in advance. Hoi An Ancient Town is best experienced on foot – the hotel should ideally be within walking distance or a short taxi ride.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided walking tour of Hoi An Ancient Town UNESCO World Heritage Site – visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (Lai Vien Kieu), the Assembly Hall of the Fujian Chinese Congregation, and Tan Ky Ancient House. Learn about the town's 15th-century trading port history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Attend a premium hands-on Vietnamese cooking class at a riverside school (Red Bridge Cooking School recommended) – visit the local market with the chef, learn to make Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature noodle dish), White Rose Dumplings, and crispy Banh Xeo pancakes.
day_by_day.evening: Release a traditional paper lantern on the Thu Bon River during the monthly Lantern Festival (check dates) or watch local lantern sellers illuminate the riverbanks. Explore the Night Market on An Hoi Island.

meals.breakfast: Cao Lau at Thanh Cao Lau – the only place serving authentic Cao Lau made with water from the town's ancient Cham wells.
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared and enjoyed during your cooking class experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mango Mango Restaurant – a sophisticated rooftop dining experience with creative Vietnamese-fusion cuisine and panoramic Ancient Town views.

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An's Ancient Town restricts motorbike access during certain hours – walking is the best way to explore. The full moon lantern festival occurs monthly; check if it aligns with your visit for a magical experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise tour to My Son Sanctuary – a UNESCO World Heritage Site of ancient Cham Hindu temples dating to the 4th–14th centuries. Arrive before the tour groups for a serene, atmospheric experience among the jungle ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Bicycle through the lush Hoi An countryside – ride through rice paddies, visit a traditional farming village, and explore the Tra Que Vegetable Village where organic herbs used in Hoi An's cuisine are grown. Try your hand at traditional farming techniques with local farmers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hoi An for a bespoke tailoring fitting appointment – Hoi An is world-famous for its skilled tailors who can create custom garments in 24–48 hours. Browse the silk shops on Le Loi Street.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong – possibly the most famous Banh Mi in Vietnam, a Hoi An institution featured in countless food guides.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in the countryside during the cycling tour – fresh Vietnamese sandwiches, tropical fruits, and coconut water.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Streets Restaurant – a social enterprise training disadvantaged youth in hospitality, serving exceptional Vietnamese cuisine in an elegant garden setting.

day_by_day.notes: My Son is best visited at sunrise to avoid heat and crowds. Bring insect repellent and sun protection for the countryside cycling tour. Place your tailor order today to allow time for fittings before departure.

day_by_day.date: Day 8 – April 22, 2027 (Da Nang & Ba Na Hills)
day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Da Nang (45 minutes). Visit the Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son) – a cluster of five marble and limestone hills with ancient Buddhist sanctuaries, caves, and panoramic coastal views. Climb to the summit for sweeping views of Da Nang Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ba Na Hills via the world record-breaking cable car (longest non-stop single track cable car). Explore the French Village, the iconic Golden Bridge held by giant stone hands, and the Fantasy Park. The cooler mountain air (1,487m elevation) provides a refreshing contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hoi An. Collect tailored garments from your tailor for final fitting adjustments. Farewell dinner in Hoi An before preparing for the next destination.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Hoi An.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ba Na Hills – French-inspired brasserie cuisine at the hilltop village restaurant with mountain views.
meals.dinner: Final Hoi An dinner at Nha Hang Yaly – a beautifully restored merchant house restaurant serving refined Central Vietnamese cuisine, including local specialties like Banh Vac (white rose dumplings) and Hoi An-style grilled meats.

day_by_day.notes: Ba Na Hills can be crowded on weekends – consider visiting on a weekday. The Golden Bridge is particularly photogenic in morning light. Collect tailored items and pack them carefully for onward travel.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hoi An hotel. Transfer to Da Nang Airport for morning domestic flight to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Upon arrival, private luxury transfer to premium hotel in District 1 (Dong Khoi area recommended). Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided cultural tour of central Saigon – visit the Reunification Palace (Independence Palace), the historic Notre-Dame Cathedral of Saigon (exterior), the Central Post Office designed by Gustave Eiffel, and the iconic Ben Thanh Market for a curated shopping experience.
day_by_day.evening: Premium rooftop cocktail experience at Saigon Saigon Bar at the Caravelle Hotel – a legendary Saigon institution with history dating to the Vietnam War era. Watch the dazzling city lights of Ho Chi Minh City from the 9th floor.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Hoi An before departure.
meals.lunch: Banh Mi Huynh Hoa – widely considered Saigon's finest Banh Mi, packed with premium cold cuts, pate, and fresh herbs.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuc Gach Quan – a stunning converted French villa restaurant serving traditional Southern Vietnamese home-style cooking in an antique-filled, garden setting. A favorite of discerning locals and international food critics.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh City traffic can be intense – allow extra travel time between sites. The Reunification Palace requires modest dress. Book Cuc Gach Quan well in advance as it fills up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day premium Mekong Delta tour departing early. Cruise the waterways of the Mekong Delta by traditional wooden boat – visit floating markets (Cai Be or Cai Rang), tropical fruit orchards, a traditional rice paper and coconut candy factory, and a honey bee farm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Mekong exploration – cycle through delta villages on narrow paths between rice paddies and fruit gardens. Interact with local farming families and experience authentic rural southern Vietnamese life far removed from city tourism.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ho Chi Minh City by late afternoon. Final evening at leisure – last-minute shopping on Dong Khoi Street or Le Thanh Ton Street (Little Tokyo) for Vietnamese silk, lacquerware, and coffee. Farewell dinner at the city's finest establishment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Ho Chi Minh City before early departure.
meals.lunch: Traditional Mekong Delta lunch at a riverside family home – fresh elephant ear fish (Ca Tai Tuong), hot pot, seasonal vegetables, and fresh coconut water straight from the tree.
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner at The Deck Saigon – an elegant open-air riverside restaurant with spectacular views of the Saigon River, serving premium Vietnamese and international cuisine. Finish with Vietnamese specialty desserts and a final Vietnamese iced coffee.

day_by_day.notes: Depart for the Mekong Delta by 07:00 to reach the floating markets at their most active (before 09:00). Pack light for the boat tour. Arrange airport transfer for departure day through your hotel. Purchase Vietnamese coffee, pho spice kits, and silk as premium souvenirs.
